The refactor is directionally sound: moving the per-test `Mock(ServiceClass)` reassignment into a single fixture, and relying on `Mock(spec=...)` auto-detecting `async def` methods (which become awaitable `AsyncMock` children) so handlers can actually `await` them. One functional gap: the stated goal of supporting pool permissions isn't delivered. `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock.__getattr__` still resolves every accessor to a boolean (`item in self._permissions`), so methods like `list_pools_with_view_machines_access` return `False` rather than a list of pool IDs. The new `endpoints_with_authentication_only` fixture in test_machines tries to paper over this but does it ineffectively (see inline). The `filterwarnings` in base.py is a pragmatic but broad suppression of unawaited-coroutine warnings that can mask real regressions in these auth tests. Secondary: `create_services_mock` now eagerly materializes ~70 spec'd mocks per test (function-scoped), most unused, and is brittle to future non-class annotations.

src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/public/ha.213: These `list_pools_*` return values are set on the default `get_client.return_value` MagicMock, but `mocked_api_client_user_with_permissions()` reinstalls `openfga_tuples.get_client.return_value = AsyncOpenFGAClientMock(...)` when the test runs, discarding this setup. The machines list handler then gets `False` from `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock.__getattr__` for each pool accessor and executes `set(False)`, raising TypeError (500). Since the base assertion only excludes 401/403, the auth-only test passes without exercising a happy-path 200. Configure the pool accessors on the client the factory actually installs, or make `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock` return lists for pool-list accessors.

src/tests/fixtures/__init__.py.70: Building the mock from `ServiceCollectionV3.__annotations__` works today only because every annotation is a concrete service class; any future non-class annotation (`Optional[...]`, `ClassVar`, a bare type) makes `Mock(service_class)` raise TypeError at fixture setup. It also eagerly constructs ~70 spec'd `Mock(...)` objects for every test that requests `services_mock`, most of which go unused; `Mock(spec=Class)` recursively introspects the full class, so this can materially slow the suite. Consider lazy creation or guarding non-class entries.
